**Back up first.** Mount the device (hold Button 1 / KEY0 while plugging in USB if it doesn't appear) and copy its entire contents somewhere safe, so you can recover or revert to OEM firmware later.

Then download from the Assets below:

name: v1.14.0
body:
✅ **Stable Release**

# What's New

1. CC INC/DEC: Increment/decrement CC values on each press.
    - Step mode: Set the amount each press increases/decreases the current CC value by.
    - Slot mode: Up to 16 slots with their own LED color and name, so "Clean / Crunch / Lead" scrolls under your foot and the LED and screen says which one you're on.
1. Off Color: Set a custom color for a button's "OFF" state, instead of just dim/off.
1. CC Listen: Set a button to send one CC value but listen for inbound changes on another. This is great for loopers that trigger on one CC but send another when their state changes.
1. MIDI Ring Support: Support daisy-chaining multiple Captains into a ring without creating a feedback loop. This enables bi-directional control over a DIN connection!
1. Save & Restart in GUI: The GUI's Save button now offers a Save & Restart option to speed up your config workflow!

## Bug Fixes

1. Fixed an issue where messages forwarded on the DIN ports were forced to Channel 1.
1. Fixed an issue where restarts would hang
1. Additional cleanup and tweaks

The manual and documentation are starting to take shape. It's very much not complete, but check out the current content: https://mc-music-workshop.github.io/midi-captain-max/docs/

name: v1.14.0-rc.1
body:
🚀 **Release Candidate** - Final testing before stable release.

## What's New Since v1.13.1

### CC+ / CC- buttons

Step a value with your foot instead of just toggling it. A **CC+** or **CC-** button moves a shared CC value up or down on each press, in whichever of two flavors suits the job:

- **Step**: a fixed step size within a min/max range, optionally wrapping. The display shows the live value (`CC7=64`).
- **Slots**: 2–16 equal-size slots with their own LED color and name, so "Clean / Crunch / Lead" scrolls under your foot and the LED and screen say which one you're on.

The value is shared by every CC+/CC- button on every page and survives page switches, so an up button and a down button drive the same value — and your host can set it too, just by sending that CC.

### A distinct off color per button

A toggle button used to have one color, with "off" being a dimmed or extinguished version of it. Set **LED Off Color** and you get two: green when on, blue when off, both at full brightness. Leave it alone and nothing changes.

### Listen on a different CC than you send

Some hosts take commands on one CC and report state on another — a looper's play trigger versus its is-playing indicator — so the LED could never follow what was actually happening. Fill in **Listen CC** and the button sends on its own CC but takes its state from that one. The host owns the LED from then on, so foot and host stop disagreeing.

### MIDI ring rigs: multiple Captains, all in sync

Daisy-chaining Captains over 5-pin DIN is one-way, so only the USB-connected pedal ever heard the host. The routing matrix now has a **This pedal** row and column, which lets you close the chain into a ring where every pedal hears the host. Turn off three routes on the pedal that closes the ring and its own messages stop lapping the ring and reaching the host twice.

### Save to Device / Save & Restart

The Save button is now split. Pick **Save to Device** or **Save & Restart** once and your choice sticks — including for ⌘S — instead of being asked about restarting on every single save.

## Fixes

- **MIDI thru no longer flattens forwarded messages onto channel 1** — messages keep the channel they arrived on.
- **Save & Restart actually restarts**, and no longer hangs or aborts partway through the reboot.
- **ONE and DUO2 no longer come up blank** — the current CC+/CC- slot shows on the display at boot and after page switches.
- **No more crash on the second CC+/CC- press** in a keytimes button using slots.
- **Labels update without touching flash mid-performance** — display glyphs are preloaded at boot.
- **Switching a button from keytimes back to single press** no longer leaves the editor stuck on "Fix errors to save" with nothing to fix.

## New documentation

Five user guides are now published, all built around the Config Editor rather than raw JSON:

- [Installation](https://mc-music-workshop.github.io/midi-captain-max/docs/installation)
- [Keytimes: one button, several jobs](https://mc-music-workshop.github.io/midi-captain-max/docs/keytimes)
- [Inbound MIDI: host-to-device button sync](https://mc-music-workshop.github.io/midi-captain-max/docs/inbound-midi)
- [MIDI routing matrix](https://mc-music-workshop.github.io/midi-captain-max/docs/midi-thru)
- [Page control via MIDI-IN](https://mc-music-workshop.github.io/midi-captain-max/docs/page-control)

## What's Changed
* Host-driven LEDs, per-button off colors, MIDI ring rigs, and two MIDI thru / Save & Restart fixes by @mcascone in https://github.com/MC-Music-Workshop/midi-captain-max/pull/197


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/MC-Music-Workshop/midi-captain-max/compare/v1.14.0-beta.5...v1.14.0-rc.1

name: v1.14.0-beta.5
body:
🧪 **Beta Release** - Feature complete, undergoing final testing. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/MC-Music-Workshop/midi-captain-max/compare/v1.14.0-beta.4...v1.14.0-beta.5 ## First: Backup! *Before doing any of this, if you haven't already, please back up your existing config and firmware to a safe place* for recovery or to revert to OEM firmware: 1. Mount the device to your computer. You may have to hold down Button 1 / KEY0 to force it to mount. 2. Copy all contents of the device to a safe place on your computer. # Installation Once MIDI Captain MAX is installed, manual firmware updates are no longer needed. The GUI Config Editor now includes a **Firmware Installation** section at the bottom of the window. It shows the currently installed firmware version and the bundled version available to install. You can download either: - The appropriate Config Editor installer for your OS: `.dmg` for macOS, `.exe` or `.msi` for Windows, `.AppImage` (portable) or `.deb` (Debian/Ubuntu) for Linux. **The Config Editor includes the bundled firmware, so you don't need to download it separately**, or - The `MIDI-Captain-MAX-v1.14.0-beta.5-complete.zip` package if you want the GUI and the firmware as separate packages.
For example, if you prefer the deploy script, or are on an unsupported OS, this package includes everything you need. (The GUI still includes the bundled firmware; the zip is just for convenience if you want to use the deploy script instead of the GUI installer.) ## Updating an Existing MIDI Captain MAX Install 1. Connect your MIDI Captain via USB and power it on. - The device may mount as `CIRCUITPY` or `MIDICAPTAIN`. - If no drive appears, hold switch 1 / KEY0 while plugging in USB. 2. Install and open the MIDI Captain MAX Config Editor. 3. Scroll to the **Firmware Installation** section at the bottom of the app window. 4. Click **Install Firmware**. By default, the installer preserves your existing `config.json`. Enable **Reset config.json to bundled defaults** only if you want to overwrite your current settings with the default template. The app will copy the firmware, reload the device, and update it in place. ## First Run of the Config Editor The first time you use the page-template feature (**Edit Pages… → Save as template… / Add from template…**), the editor creates a folder in your Documents: - `Documents/MIDICaptainMAX/templates`: your saved page templates. The save dialog and the template picker both point here by default. - `Documents/MIDICaptainMAX/pages`: reserved for saved pages. Templates are plain JSON files, one page each — feel free to back them up, rename them in Finder/Explorer, or share them with other MIDI Captain users. ## First Run on OEM Firmware If your MIDI Captain is still running the factory Paint Audio firmware, the Config Editor may show `OEM (no VERSION.txt file)`. The deploy script is no longer required — the entire first install can be done from the Config Editor. The installer only needs to know your device type, and you tell it that by saving a config from the editor first: 1. Hold Button 1 / KEY0 while plugging in USB to enter the OEM USB settings mode. A `MIDICAPTAIN` drive should appear. 2. Open the Config Editor and select the device. Since there's no MAX `config.json` on the drive yet, the editor starts a fresh default config. 3. Set **Device Type** to your model and click **Save to Device**. 4. Scroll to the **Firmware Installation** section and click **Install Firmware**. For a first install, enable **Reset config.json to bundled defaults** so you start from the full default template for your device. - If the button blocks with a CircuitPython version error, see the next section, then come back. ### If the Config Editor shows a CircuitPython version error (2026-batch devices) 2026-batch devices shipped with CP 9.2.7. The **Install Firmware** button will block with a version error. Fix this first: 1. In the **Firmware Installation** section, open **Advanced / Recovery**. 2. Click **Reflash CircuitPython 7.3.1**. The editor sends a command over serial, reboots the device into its RP2040 bootloader, copies the bundled `.uf2`, and waits for `CIRCUITPY` to remount — no physical button hold needed. 3. Once `CIRCUITPY` remounts, continue with the first-install steps above (the device is already mounted; skip step 1). If the editor can't reach the device over serial, see the [manual bootloader entry guide](https://github.com/MC-Music-Workshop/midi-captain-max/blob/main/docs/recovery-bootloader-entry.md) (doc pending) ### Deploy script (alternative) Prefer the command line, or on an OS the GUI doesn't support? The deploy script still performs a full first install: 1. Hold Button 1 / KEY0 while plugging in USB to enter the OEM USB settings mode. A `MIDICAPTAIN` drive should appear. 2. Download and extract `MIDI-Captain-MAX-v1.14.0-beta.5-complete.zip` from the Assets section below. 3. Run the included deploy script once with your device type:
_NOTE: only enter the desired device type, not the full list of options.
For example, if you have a Nano 4, run `./deploy.sh --device nano4`_. - macOS / Linux: `./deploy.sh --device std10|mini6|nano4|duo2|one1` - Windows PowerShell: `.\deploy.ps1 -Device std10|mini6|nano4|duo2|one1` - Windows cmd (if PowerShell blocks unsigned scripts): `deploy.bat -Device std10|mini6|nano4|duo2|one1` — invokes `deploy.ps1` with a per-process `ExecutionPolicy Bypass`; does not change any system policy. 4. Reconnect the device and open the MIDI Captain MAX Config Editor. 5. From then on, use the **Firmware Installation** section in the app for future updates. ## Recovery If anything goes wrong, it is fully recoverable: 1. Mount the device. 2. Erase the contents. 3. Restore your backup, or re-run the first-install steps above.

🧪 **Beta Release** - Feature complete, undergoing final testing. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/MC-Music-Workshop/midi-captain-max/compare/v1.140.0-beta.1...v1.14.0-beta.2 ## First: Backup! *Before doing any of this, if you haven't already, please back up your existing config and firmware to a safe place* for recovery or to revert to OEM firmware: 1. Mount the device to your computer. You may have to hold down Button 1 / KEY0 to force it to mount. 2. Copy all contents of the device to a safe place on your computer. # Installation Once MIDI Captain MAX is installed, manual firmware updates are no longer needed. The GUI Config Editor now includes a **Firmware Installation** section at the bottom of the window. It shows the currently installed firmware version and the bundled version available to install. You can download either: - The appropriate Config Editor installer for your OS: `.dmg` for macOS, `.exe` or `.msi` for Windows, `.AppImage` (portable) or `.deb` (Debian/Ubuntu) for Linux. **The Config Editor includes the bundled firmware, so you don't need to download it separately**, or - The `MIDI-Captain-MAX-v1.14.0-beta.2-complete.zip` package if you want the GUI and the firmware as separate packages.
For example, if you prefer the deploy script, or are on an unsupported OS, this package includes everything you need. (The GUI still includes the bundled firmware; the zip is just for convenience if you want to use the deploy script instead of the GUI installer.) ## Updating an Existing MIDI Captain MAX Install 1. Connect your MIDI Captain via USB and power it on. - The device may mount as `CIRCUITPY` or `MIDICAPTAIN`. - If no drive appears, hold switch 1 / KEY0 while plugging in USB. 2. Install and open the MIDI Captain MAX Config Editor. 3. Scroll to the **Firmware Installation** section at the bottom of the app window. 4. Click **Install Firmware**. By default, the installer preserves your existing `config.json`. Enable **Reset config.json to bundled defaults** only if you want to overwrite your current settings with the default template. The app will copy the firmware, reload the device, and update it in place. ## First Run of the Config Editor The first time you use the page-template feature (**Edit Pages… → Save as template… / Add from template…**), the editor creates a folder in your Documents: - `Documents/MIDICaptainMAX/templates`: your saved page templates. The save dialog and the template picker both point here by default. - `Documents/MIDICaptainMAX/pages`: reserved for saved pages. Templates are plain JSON files, one page each — feel free to back them up, rename them in Finder/Explorer, or share them with other MIDI Captain users. ## First Run on OEM Firmware If your MIDI Captain is still running the factory Paint Audio firmware, the Config Editor may show `OEM (no VERSION.txt file)`. The deploy script is no longer required — the entire first install can be done from the Config Editor. The installer only needs to know your device type, and you tell it that by saving a config from the editor first: 1. Hold Button 1 / KEY0 while plugging in USB to enter the OEM USB settings mode. A `MIDICAPTAIN` drive should appear. 2. Open the Config Editor and select the device. Since there's no MAX `config.json` on the drive yet, the editor starts a fresh default config. 3. Set **Device Type** to your model and click **Save to Device**. 4. Scroll to the **Firmware Installation** section and click **Install Firmware**. For a first install, enable **Reset config.json to bundled defaults** so you start from the full default template for your device. - If the button blocks with a CircuitPython version error, see the next section, then come back. ### If the Config Editor shows a CircuitPython version error (2026-batch devices) 2026-batch devices shipped with CP 9.2.7. The **Install Firmware** button will block with a version error. Fix this first: 1. In the **Firmware Installation** section, open **Advanced / Recovery**. 2. Click **Reflash CircuitPython 7.3.1**. The editor sends a command over serial, reboots the device into its RP2040 bootloader, copies the bundled `.uf2`, and waits for `CIRCUITPY` to remount — no physical button hold needed. 3. Once `CIRCUITPY` remounts, continue with the first-install steps above (the device is already mounted; skip step 1). If the editor can't reach the device over serial, see the [manual bootloader entry guide](https://github.com/MC-Music-Workshop/midi-captain-max/blob/main/docs/recovery-bootloader-entry.md) (doc pending) ### Deploy script (alternative) Prefer the command line, or on an OS the GUI doesn't support? The deploy script still performs a full first install: 1. Hold Button 1 / KEY0 while plugging in USB to enter the OEM USB settings mode. A `MIDICAPTAIN` drive should appear. 2. Download and extract `MIDI-Captain-MAX-v1.14.0-beta.2-complete.zip` from the Assets section below. 3. Run the included deploy script once with your device type:
_NOTE: only enter the desired device type, not the full list of options.
For example, if you have a Nano 4, run `./deploy.sh --device nano4`_. - macOS / Linux: `./deploy.sh --device std10|mini6|nano4|duo2|one1` - Windows PowerShell: `.\deploy.ps1 -Device std10|mini6|nano4|duo2|one1` - Windows cmd (if PowerShell blocks unsigned scripts): `deploy.bat -Device std10|mini6|nano4|duo2|one1` — invokes `deploy.ps1` with a per-process `ExecutionPolicy Bypass`; does not change any system policy. 4. Reconnect the device and open the MIDI Captain MAX Config Editor. 5. From then on, use the **Firmware Installation** section in the app for future updates. ## Recovery If anything goes wrong, it is fully recoverable: 1. Mount the device. 2. Erase the contents. 3. Restore your backup, or re-run the first-install steps above.
